question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-1R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z&=1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-3-(0)(4)=-3 \\ x&=1-(2)(-3)-(1)(4)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,-3,4\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-6y&=-9 \\ 2x-3y+z&=-2 \\ -2x+5y+2z&=11\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 0 & -9 \\ 2 & -3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & -3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y&=-3 \\ y+z&=4 \\ z&=1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=1 \\ y&=4-(1)(1)=3 \\ x&=-3-(-2)(3)-(0)(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,3,1\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-4z&=-4 \\ -x+y-4z&=-7 \\ x+y+z&=1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 0 & -4 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & -4 & -7 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -4 & -7 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2z&=2 \\ y-2z&=-5 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-5-(-2)(4)=3 \\ x&=2-(0)(3)-(2)(4)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -6,3,4\rangle$.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 6 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 6 & 6 \\ -1 & 4 & 0 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 6 & 6 \\ -1 & 4 & 0 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ -1 & 4 & 0 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+2z&=0 \\ y+2z&=6 \\ z&=2\end{aligned}\right..

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=2 \\ y&=6-(2)(2)=2 \\ x&=0-(-2)(2)-(2)(2)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 0,2,2\rangle$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -4 & 2 & 8 \\ 2 & 5 & -2 & -9 \\ -2 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -4 \\ 2 & 5 & -2 & -9 \\ -2 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z&=-4 \\ y&=-1 \\ z&=-4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-4 \\ y&=-1-(0)(-4)=-1 \\ x&=-4-(2)(-1)-(-1)(-4)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -6,-1,-4\rangle$.

The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 6 & 0 & -12 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & -3 & -1 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & -3 & -1 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & -1 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y&=-4 \\ y-2z&=0 \\ z&=-3\end{aligned}\right..

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-3 \\ y&=0-(-2)(-3)=-6 \\ x&=-4-(2)(-6)-(0)(-3)=8.\end{aligned}

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 8,-6,-3\rangle$.
